episodes.192343: A cold front moving into an area of extreme heat, generated a line of thunderstorms with strong damaging winds.
episodes.192413: A cluster of severe thunderstorms moved up along the SC coast ahead of a cold front that interacted with a warm and extremely humid airmass.
episodes.192762: A cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms rolled through much of southeast Arizona resulting in flash flooding including swift water rescues and damaging winds.
episodes.192785: High pressure system to the south of Nevada created a weak flow pattern over the area that still had excess moisture from monsoonal storm pattern earlier in the week which elevated conditions to produce thunderstorms, some reaching severe.
episodes.193131: Sufficient moisture in combination with a shortwave impulse brushing by the area resulted in numerous strong thunderstorm wind gusts in addition to isolated instances of flash flooding.
episodes.193147: An isolated thunderstorm produced a severe wind gust.
episodes.193184: Thunderstorms with heavy rainfall occurred in central Goshen County, including Torrington where numerous reports of flash flooding were received. This included portions of Highway 26 underwater.
episodes.193485: The highly favorable flash flooding environment continued for another day on 7-25 with high precipitable water over 2.25 inches, parallel deep layer shear to the low level moisture convergence boundary, and moderate instability aloft. High rainfall rates exceeding 2 inches per hour and a series of training thunderstorms caused localized flash flood in the greater Newberry area.
episodes.194490: In the morning, thunderstorms developed along the land breeze just off the Charleston County coast. Later that day in the evening, inland thunderstorms moved to the east across the Charleston County coast and the adjacent coastal waters. The main threat with these thunderstorms was strong wind gusts.
episodes.194492: Isolated to scattered thunderstorms developed across portions of southeast South Carolina in the late afternoon hours and produced strong, gusty winds.
episodes.194493: Isolated to scattered thunderstorms developed across portions of southeast Georgia in the late afternoon hours. A couple of these thunderstorms became strong enough to produce gusty winds and cloud to ground lightning strikes. One storm interacted with a nearby mesoscale boundary and prompted a Tornado Warning across Chatham County. A funnel cloud was reported on two different occasions, but the storm did not produce any known damage.
episodes.194576: With the subtropical high pressure centered near the Lower Colorado River Valley, the steering flow pattern across much of eastern and central AZ was from the north to northeast. Thunderstorm activity developed across the Mogollon Rim during the late morning into the early afternoon hours and was steered south to southwestward into south-central AZ. An upper-level disturbance moving in from New Mexico helped enhance the vertical ascent and thus resulted in the thunderstorm coverage to become quite numerous with deep and colliding outflow boundaries helping to spark new activity across the lower deserts of south-central AZ. MLCAPE values were in the 1000-1500 J/KG range, with DCAPE values of around 1500 J/KG. Thus the parameters were favorable for these thunderstorms to generate strong to severe downburst winds. The steering flow was very light, resulting in slow storm motions and thus heavy rainfall leading to isolated instances of flash flooding.
episodes.194595: A frontal boundary across southernmost portions of Missouri and Kentucky became a focal point for developing afternoon thunderstorms on the 26th, with progression slowly expanding northward. One of these storms just south of Cairo, Illinois in Mississippi County, Missouri produced a brief landspout tornado with multiple reports submitted with pictures. MLCAPE was 2000 J/kg while shear and helicity were very limited.
episodes.194631: A waterspout was observed on Mobile Bay.
episodes.194729: High based thunderstorms brought high winds to portions of Teton and Sublette Counties. The wind gusted as high as 60 mph.
episodes.194920: A broad complex of showers and thunderstorms with associated heavy rainfall developed across areas of Deep East Texas and West Central Louisiana by mid to late morning on July 26th. This occurred within an elongated axis of upper-level energy observed along much of the middle and upper Texas coast and up across interior areas of East Texas around the eastern flank of a broader mid-level trough over the Southern Plains. This energy interacted with a very deep tropical air mass and axis of stronger instability that was pooled up across the northwest Gulf of Mexico and farther inland to a lesser extent. MLCAPE values of 1500 to 2500 J/kg were noted across these areas with precipitable water values of 2 to 2.25 inches. As a result, multiple reports of flash flooding were received across parts of West Central Louisiana.
episodes.194921: A broad complex of showers and thunderstorms with associated heavy rainfall developed across areas of Deep East Texas and West Central Louisiana by mid to late morning on July 26th. This occurred within an elongated axis of upper-level energy observed along much of the middle and upper Texas coast and up across interior areas of East Texas around the eastern flank of a broader mid-level trough over the Southern Plains. This energy interacted with a very deep tropical air mass and axis of stronger instability that was pooled up across the northwest Gulf of Mexico and farther inland to a lesser extent. MLCAPE values of 1500 to 2500 J/kg were noted across these areas with precipitable water values of 2 to 2.25 inches. As a result, multiple reports of flash flooding were received across parts of Deep East Texas.
episodes.195073: Thunderstorms initiated across southeast Louisiana during the afternoon once the area reached the convective temperature. Due to multiple rounds of rainfall from these storms, New Orleans experienced flash flooding during the evening before the activity waned off shortly after sunset.
episodes.195191: Deep monsoon moisture over northern Arizona produced scattered showers and thunderstorms. One storm north of Swnoflake produced a landspout north of Snowflake.
episodes.195243: Several 50 knot plus severe thunderstorm wind gusts occurred.
